entries.title: Anthropic streaming and JSON tool actions
entries.entrypoint: POST /anthropic/v1/messages
entries.privileges: The broker may release a complete action to the Claude client after policy and receipt commit.
entries.enforcement_point: Anthropic protocol gate, canonical ActionIntent policy, receipt-bound approval
entries.containment_boundary: Protocol mediation only; actual execution containment depends on the client runtime.
entries.receipt_coverage: Requested, approval_pending, denied, released, result_observed, or outcome_unknown.
entries.failure_behavior: Malformed, unknown, disconnected, or unrecordable actions fail closed.
entries.evidence: Policy and durable receipts are tested; protocol governance alone does not contain native client execution.

entries.title: OpenAI Responses compatibility actions
entries.entrypoint: POST /openai/v1/responses
entries.privileges: Compatibility broker can release actions to an isolated Codex client configuration.
entries.enforcement_point: OpenAI protocol gate and canonical policy adapter
entries.containment_boundary: Not certified against a real current OpenAI provider stream.
entries.receipt_coverage: Compatibility decision coverage; complete production receipt correlation is not claimed.
entries.failure_behavior: Unknown actionable item types and malformed arguments fail closed.
entries.evidence: Codex remains compatibility-only until provider-backed certification.

entries.title: Explicitly degraded Claude host demo
entries.entrypoint: kerna claude --host-demo and kerna demo start
entries.privileges: The current demo launches the npm Claude executable as a host process in a disposable clone.
entries.enforcement_point: Model-seam policy observes model-issued actions, but cannot mediate every native client side effect.
entries.containment_boundary: Disposable clone only; no complete OS/container boundary around the Claude host process.
entries.receipt_coverage: Model-seam actions may be receipted; native actions outside the seam are not guaranteed to be observed.
entries.failure_behavior: The CLI prints a degraded-containment warning; this path is excluded from production and pilot claims.
entries.evidence: The host path now requires an explicit --host-demo flag and prints that it is not structurally contained.

entries.title: Governed MCP gateway calls
entries.entrypoint: MCP tools/call over stdio or direct gateway
entries.privileges: Gateway may invoke only registered tools within policy, manifest, budget, folder, and secret grants.
entries.enforcement_point: Gateway canonical arguments, permission engine, single-use approval, mandatory receipts
entries.containment_boundary: Docker is default; explicitly configured native servers run with host process authority.
entries.receipt_coverage: Gateway sessions, decisions, approvals, result digests, and terminal state are durable.
entries.failure_behavior: Unknown, denied, expired, over-budget, or unrecordable calls do not execute.
entries.evidence: Governance is strong, but a configured native runtime is not a containment boundary.

entries.title: MCP server process launch
entries.entrypoint: gateway server startup
entries.privileges: Docker servers receive declared mounts and secrets; native servers inherit restricted but host-level process execution.
entries.enforcement_point: Production manifest verification, capability validation, runtime-mode selection
entries.containment_boundary: Pinned Docker image and disjoint mounts for production; no structural containment in native mode.
entries.receipt_coverage: Tool calls are receipted; server process startup itself is operational evidence rather than an action receipt.
entries.failure_behavior: Invalid production manifests fail closed; approved native configurations can still execute on the host.
entries.evidence: Native mode is an intentional compatibility path but cannot support a contained production claim.

entries.title: Contained filesystem tool pack
entries.entrypoint: fs_read, fs_write, and fs_move gateway tools
entries.privileges: Resolved grant root with declared read-only or read-write authority.
entries.enforcement_point: Canonical root resolution, traversal rejection, symlink containment, permission and approval checks
entries.containment_boundary: Canonical filesystem root and Docker mount when the gateway runs contained.
entries.receipt_coverage: Gateway receipt records decision and result digest without content.
entries.failure_behavior: Unknown roots, traversal, absolute paths, symlink escapes, and read-only writes fail closed.
entries.evidence: Path resolution and real read/write behavior have direct tests.

entries.title: Wasmer and Tenki sandbox execution
entries.entrypoint: kerna_sandbox_run and POST /kerna/sandbox
entries.privileges: Wasmer Node bridge or authenticated Tenki worker executes bounded Python code.
entries.enforcement_point: Kerna pre-execution admission, backend allowlist, timeout, output cap, receipt commit
entries.containment_boundary: Wasmer runtime or Tenki remote sandbox; keyword admission is defense-in-depth, not containment.
entries.receipt_coverage: Blocked, completed, and failed sandbox runs persist redacted digests and backend-contacted state.
entries.failure_behavior: Escape intent is denied before backend contact; timeouts and oversized output fail safely.
entries.evidence: Containment is delegated; artifact provenance and physical macOS verification remain.

entries.title: Legacy task scheduler and repository command execution
entries.entrypoint: kerna run and routine run
entries.privileges: Legacy scheduler can coordinate provider and MCP operations using the current Kerna process configuration.
entries.enforcement_point: Permission engine, budgets, sandbox configuration, and MCP gateway
entries.containment_boundary: Docker is the configured default, but legacy paths are not the supported Guard front door.
entries.receipt_coverage: Task, tool, budget, and event records exist; they do not equal complete native-agent action coverage.
entries.failure_behavior: Policy and budgets abort known calls; unknown legacy composition requires containment review.
entries.evidence: The legacy action-capable agent loop remains excluded as a product front door. Its new ask_text entrypoint supplies no tool schemas and rejects any provider-returned action.

entries.title: Provider and local-model HTTP forwarding
entries.entrypoint: provider resolution, broker forwarding, model detection, and validation
entries.privileges: Trusted broker holds provider keys and can contact configured provider or loopback Ollama endpoints.
entries.enforcement_point: Provider configuration validation, route resolution, URL construction, bounded HTTP clients
entries.containment_boundary: Broker egress; the agent receives only a Kerna session credential.
entries.receipt_coverage: Session and route outcomes are recorded; provider prose and keys are not persisted.
entries.failure_behavior: Missing keys, invalid routes, remote local-only endpoints, and timeouts fail closed.
entries.evidence: Guard broker traffic now uses exact host allowlists, HTTPS/port enforcement, one-time DNS validation with pinned addresses, ambient-proxy removal, redirect refusal, and private/reserved address denial. Legacy provider clients remain outside the Guard production path.

entries.title: Secret injection and credential storage
entries.entrypoint: provider keys, plugin secrets, and demo hidden prompts
entries.privileges: Trusted Kerna process reads or injects declared secrets into the intended broker or plugin process.
entries.enforcement_point: Declared-secret filtering, secret-name-only Docker arguments, raw-key persistence prohibition, value-aware output redaction, separate agent/control credentials
entries.containment_boundary: Process boundary; effective only if the receiving process is itself contained.
entries.receipt_coverage: Secret values are redacted; presence and routing may be represented without value retention.
entries.failure_behavior: Undeclared secrets are withheld, secret values are absent from Docker command arguments, plugin output containing raw or reversibly encoded credentials is redacted, and raw API keys are not written to kerna.toml.
entries.evidence: Production plugins receive only doubly declared secrets in their contained process. Secret values are excluded from host Docker argv, undeclared values are withheld, and raw/base64/URL-safe-base64/hex/percent-encoded echoes are removed before agent delivery or receipt persistence. Native plugin mode remains development-only.

entries.title: Browser control-plane mutations
entries.entrypoint: approval, deny, stop-session, apply, and export endpoints
entries.privileges: Local control process may make approval decisions, stop sessions, export evidence, or apply reviewed output.
entries.enforcement_point: Loopback bind, exact Origin, CSRF credential, single-use approval binding, clean-target checks
entries.containment_boundary: Local browser control credential is distinct from the agent session credential.
entries.receipt_coverage: Decisions and session transitions are durable; evidence export is signed.
entries.failure_behavior: Wrong origin/token, stale binding, dirty target, or changed baseline is refused.
entries.evidence: Apply flow is trusted-host administration and must never be exposed to the agent credential.

entries.title: Worktree creation, Git inspection, and explicit apply
entries.entrypoint: guard launch and dashboard apply
entries.privileges: Trusted host supervisor invokes Git and writes disposable worktrees or explicitly approved output.
entries.enforcement_point: Canonical repository checks, recorded baseline digest, clean target, explicit control-plane action
entries.containment_boundary: Trusted supervisor, outside agent authority.
entries.receipt_coverage: Baseline and apply outcome are shown/exported; source repository remains unchanged before apply.
entries.failure_behavior: Dirty, changed, same-worktree, conflicting, or non-Git targets are refused.
entries.evidence: Trusted host Git operations are valid only when their inputs cannot be model-controlled.

entries.title: Administrative configuration and installation
entries.entrypoint: config, pack, plugin, folder, channel, key, and registry commands
entries.privileges: Interactive Kerna CLI mutates user configuration and installs reviewed local assets.
entries.enforcement_point: CLI parsing, configuration validation, signed manifests, explicit operator invocation
entries.containment_boundary: Trusted host administration; excluded from model authority.
entries.receipt_coverage: Configuration changes are not agent-action receipts.
entries.failure_behavior: Invalid manifests, grants, or provider configuration are rejected.
entries.evidence: These commands must remain unreachable from the agent plane.

entries.title: Container process sandbox
entries.entrypoint: ProcessSandbox command execution
entries.privileges: Pinned Docker image receives only declared mounts and configured network mode.
entries.enforcement_point: Docker-required runtime, immutable risk floor, package-manager classification, timeout
entries.containment_boundary: Docker Engine with pinned image; command classification is not the boundary.
entries.receipt_coverage: Scheduler/tool receipts cover admitted executions and failures.
entries.failure_behavior: Missing Docker, host paths, package-manager actions, and unsafe wrapper commands fail or require policy action.
entries.evidence: The production boundary is Docker; the demo host launcher does not yet use it for Claude.

entries.title: Plugin and model artifact acquisition
entries.entrypoint: pack install, plugin install, Ollama pull, and model discovery
entries.privileges: Trusted host can download or register executable/model artifacts.
entries.enforcement_point: Canonical immutable-reference validation, full source revision, signed manifest digest, safe model-format allowlist, exact Claude build provenance, explicit operator selection
entries.containment_boundary: Production execution admits only verified contained plugins and the reviewed Claude image. Mutable pack installation and Ollama pull remain trusted-operator demo/development administration and cannot enter the production gateway as native execution.
entries.receipt_coverage: Installation is administrative, not a model-action receipt.
entries.failure_behavior: Mutable or malformed OCI references, abbreviated revisions, unsafe/unknown model formats, invalid manifests, and mismatched Claude image provenance fail closed before production execution.
entries.evidence: Production plugins require canonical digest-pinned OCI references plus signed, fingerprint-bound manifests. The curated model catalog requires a full immutable revision and data-only safetensors/GGUF formats; Kerna does not load model files itself. The locally built Claude image is checked against exact package version and registry integrity plus contract and digest-pinned base provenance. General pack/model acquisition remains outside agent authority and outside production claims.

entries.title: Background channels, watchdog, and scheduled network activity
entries.entrypoint: configured channel polling, health checks, cron, and watchdog tasks
entries.privileges: Long-running Kerna process can contact configured endpoints and start scheduled work.
entries.enforcement_point: Operator configuration, gateway allowlists, task budgets, and process lifecycle
entries.containment_boundary: Legacy background functionality is not part of the Claude-first Guard authority.
entries.receipt_coverage: Events and task records exist; complete security-boundary evidence is not claimed.
entries.failure_behavior: Network and task errors are surfaced, but destination hardening requires review.
entries.evidence: Legacy service access is outside MVP and must not share the Guard agent authority.

entries.title: SQLite evidence store
entries.entrypoint: all task, session, approval, receipt, and event persistence
entries.privileges: Trusted Kerna process writes the configured local SQLite evidence database.
entries.enforcement_point: Broker-only state mount, trusted KERNA_DB_PATH override, prepared statements, mandatory pre-action transactions, redaction, append-only receipt hash chain
entries.containment_boundary: The evidence directory is a sibling of the disposable worktree, mounted only at /kerna-state in the broker. The agent receives only the worktree mount.
entries.receipt_coverage: This is the receipt system of record.
entries.failure_behavior: Receipt persistence failure blocks action release and visibly degrades or halts the session.
entries.evidence: The production broker gets a dedicated evidence mount outside the worktree. Static argument tests and the live Windows container probe prove the agent has neither /kerna-state nor the former workspace database path. Database concurrency, redaction, mandatory pre-release commit, and hash-chain tests remain green. Physical macOS proof is a release gate.

entries.title: Mock and conformance subprocesses
entries.entrypoint: mockmcp, conformance client, benchmark, and test fixtures
entries.privileges: Developer/test process can start local fixtures and write temporary evidence.
entries.enforcement_point: Test-only CLI paths and loopback/local fixtures
entries.containment_boundary: Not shipped as an agent-authorized production operation.
entries.receipt_coverage: Test evidence only.
entries.failure_behavior: Bounded timeouts and fixture assertions fail the test.
entries.evidence: Coverage scanner includes these files so test helpers cannot be mistaken for unclassified production surfaces.

entries.title: Production Claude agent container
entries.entrypoint: kerna claude and kerna guard claude without --host-demo
entries.privileges: The agent can write only the disposable workspace and can connect only to the Kerna broker on an internal Docker network.
entries.enforcement_point: Digest-pinned base images, exact package/base provenance labels, canonical image ID, one bind mount, read-only root, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, scoped session credential, and separate Docker networks
entries.containment_boundary: Claude runs in an agent container attached only to an internal network; the broker runs separately on both the internal and egress networks.
entries.receipt_coverage: Production native actions are protocol-gated and receipt-bound; execution remains confined to the disposable workspace. Production no longer launches an agent-local MCP gateway with evidence-store access.
entries.failure_behavior: Missing or mislabeled image, unsupported local/shadow route, Docker failure, broker failure, or network setup failure aborts before Claude starts.
entries.evidence: Windows live proof showed workspace-only write access, no evidence mount, no host home, no Docker socket, no provider/browser/plugin credential, broker reachability, and no public network. Physical macOS proof remains required before pilot GO.

entries.title: Native tool-less model question and chat
entries.entrypoint: kerna ask <question>; kerna chat
entries.privileges: The trusted Kerna CLI can send operator-authored text through a scoped localhost session; only the short-lived broker receives the provider key and provider-network egress, while the model receives no tool schemas or execution authority.
entries.enforcement_point: Provider allowlist, hidden credential prompt, stdin-only broker key injection, scoped session authentication, loopback-only publication, empty tool catalog, text-only chat history validation, incremental SSE validation, and fail-closed rejection of action-bearing, malformed, truncated, or empty responses
entries.containment_boundary: Provider credentials and outbound provider traffic are contained in a hardened broker container on a dedicated egress network. The host CLI holds only the operator prompt/history, scoped broker credential, and renderer state; no filesystem tool, process tool, MCP tool, or repository mutation is available.
entries.receipt_coverage: Prompts, chat history, and model prose are intentionally not persisted. Stable session events report start, deltas, context clearing, completion, interruption, or a redacted failure class without retaining content.
entries.failure_behavior: Empty questions, non-text/tool-shaped chat history, missing credentials, broker startup failure, Ctrl+C, provider errors, action-bearing replies, malformed or empty replies terminate without executing an action; the exact broker container and network are removed on every return path.
entries.evidence: The deterministic ask/chat mock smokes returned canonical JSONL with no TUI, prompt, transcript, or tool field. Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible fixtures produce exact text across every fixed chunk size, while action-bearing, malformed, truncated, and tool-shaped history paths fail closed. Ctrl+C emits session.interrupted and drops the same RAII broker guard used by provider failure. A Windows inert-key probe reached only the loopback broker, emitted a redacted terminal failure, and left zero native broker containers or egress networks; the provider key was supplied over stdin and absent from container arguments. Provider-backed success remains a separate live acceptance gate before release.

entries.title: Native code dry-run proposal preflight
entries.entrypoint: kerna code <goal> --repo <path>
entries.privileges: The trusted Kerna CLI runs read-only Git metadata commands on the selected repository, then asks the broker-contained model for a proposal with no tools, no patch authority, and no repository mutation authority. Proposal JSON is parsed into non-executable preflight candidates; only eligible file_read candidates continue into the SB-022 receipt-bound inspection path.
entries.enforcement_point: Git repository resolution, bounded status/file-list metadata, explicit dry-run prompt, file-content reads only through the SB-022 contained inspection path, empty tool catalog, text-only SSE validation, strict proposal envelope parsing, canonical ActionIntent normalization for proposed file/shell/network/package actions, policy preflight, broker scoped authentication, stdin-only provider key injection, and fail-closed terminal events
entries.containment_boundary: Trusted host Git metadata reads are operator-authorized administration. Provider credentials and outbound provider traffic remain in the hardened broker container. Proposed actions are not executed by the preflight itself; their required future containment is reported as contained worktree read/write, Docker process execution, broker egress, or contained package-manager execution before any later release.
entries.receipt_coverage: Goal, repository metadata, prompt, proposal text, and model prose are intentionally not persisted. Stable session events record start, deltas, proposal.preflight, completion, interruption, or redacted failure class only. Each proposal preflight action reports receipt_state=preflight_only_not_requested and executable=false; eligible file_read actions are then converted into SB-022 receipts while every other kind stays preflight-only.
entries.failure_behavior: Empty goals, non-Git repositories, Git metadata failures, missing credentials, broker startup failure, Ctrl+C, provider errors, action-bearing replies, malformed streams, empty output, missing proposal markers, malformed proposal JSON, unknown proposal fields, unknown proposal kinds, missing required action fields, and oversized proposals fail without executing a repository action; broker container and network cleanup follows the native RAII path.
entries.evidence: The dry-run prompt builder exposes only bounded Git metadata, states that no tools/shell/network/patch authority is available, and requires a strict proposal JSON block. Kerna converts supported proposed actions into canonical ActionIntent candidates, evaluates policy, and emits proposal.preflight with executable=false and receipt_state=preflight_only_not_requested. The preflight itself does not claim that a proposal has been requested, approved, receipted, released, or applied; Phase 7 converts only eligible file_read candidates into the separately receipted SB-022 inspection path.

entries.title: Native code contained read-only inspection
entries.entrypoint: kerna code <goal> --repo <path>, eligible file_read proposals
entries.privileges: The trusted Kerna CLI may read one repository file inside the resolved Git worktree boundary after policy allow, canonical path validation, and durable receipt commit, returning a bounded preview with a content digest and byte count only.
entries.enforcement_point: file_read-only eligibility, canonical ActionIntent policy allow, relative-path-only validation, Windows drive/UNC/verbatim and home-reference rejection, component traversal rejection, reserved device-name rejection, canonicalized symlink containment strictly inside the Git worktree root, .git-internals rejection on proposed and resolved paths, secret-path rejection on proposed and resolved paths, evidence-database and SQLite sidecar rejection, regular-file check, 512 KiB file-size cap, receipt-bound requested+released commit before the file is opened, result_observed advancement with digest-only details, explicit outcome_unknown downgrade, and per-action fail-closed blocking
entries.containment_boundary: Trusted host CLI process with canonical path validation. No Docker or agent-container boundary is claimed for this phase: reads are limited to canonical paths strictly inside the resolved Git worktree, and writes, shell, network, package, and patch authority remain unavailable. Trusted-host Git metadata administration (SB-021) stays separate from these model-controlled reads, which are receipted under the kerna_native agent identity.
entries.receipt_coverage: Each executed read commits requested and released receipt events before the file is opened, then advances to result_observed with byte count, content digest, and truncation flag. A read or observation failure after release records outcome_unknown. File content is never persisted; only digests, sizes, and bounded terminal previews are emitted. Denied, approval-required, and boundary-blocked proposals stay preflight_only_not_requested with no release receipt.
entries.failure_behavior: Unsupported action kinds, policy-denied or approval-required reads, absolute, drive, UNC, verbatim, home-relative, traversal, reserved-device, .git-internal, secret, evidence-database, missing, unresolvable, non-regular, oversized, and outside-worktree targets, and receipt-database failures all fail closed without opening the file; a released read that then fails is marked outcome_unknown rather than observed.
entries.evidence: Boundary validation is unit-tested for absolute, traversal, home, secret, device-name, .git, evidence-database, missing, oversized, non-regular, and symlink-escape targets, and the full lifecycle test proves the release receipt commits before the read and that raw file content never persists in receipts or events. The balanced policy allows ordinary repository reads while immutable invariants deny traversal and secret-path proposals before any boundary work. The inspection runs in the trusted CLI process; container containment is not claimed or credited.
